event_name: Rhinestone Cowgirls: Legendary Ladies of Country Music
blurb:
Country music has had some incredible women at the center of it for decades, and this show is built around celebrating exactly that.

Rhinestone Cowgirls: Legendary Ladies of Country Music comes to the Roswell Cultural Arts Center on November 8th, featuring three performers paying tribute to the bold voices that defined the genre. Think Dolly. Think Loretta. Think the women who built country before it was a stadium sport. The Cultural Arts Center is a proper venue for a show like this, not a bar, not a festival tent, an actual arts space where the performance is the point.

For the empty nester crowd in the Perimeter area, and for anyone who grew up with classic country in the background, this is a Sunday afternoon worth driving to Roswell for. The 4 PM start means you're home at a reasonable hour and you can make dinner out of it afterward.

Check the Roswell Cultural Arts Center for tickets and show details.
scoring_notes: Good fit for the empty nester and older adult segments of the Perimeter audience. Classic country tribute format has broad appeal for the 45-plus crowd. Sunday afternoon timing is ideal for that demographic. Roswell is a reasonable drive from the Perimeter area. Uniqueness is moderate since tribute shows are relatively common, but the specific format and venue elevate it.

event_name: Fetty Wap at Coca-Cola Roxy
blurb:
Fetty Wap had one of the more undeniable runs in mid-2010s hip hop. 'Trap Queen' was everywhere. 679 was everywhere. If you were in your mid-to-late 20s around 2015, there's a decent chance you know every word to at least three of his songs whether you planned to or not.

He's bringing that catalog to the Coca-Cola Roxy on Friday, November 6th. The Roxy is a great room for this, intimate enough that it feels like a real show rather than a stadium event, but big enough that the energy builds properly. Friday night, early-ish start at 8 PM, so you can actually make a full evening out of it.

For the Perimeter crowd who grew up with this music and now has the disposable income to actually buy good seats without thinking twice about it, this is a fun one. It's nostalgia plus a legit live performance in one of Atlanta's better mid-size venues.

Grab your tickets and make a night of it.
scoring_notes: Fetty Wap is a strong nostalgia play for the 35-42 segment of the Perimeter audience who came up with that music. Friday night is ideal timing. Uniqueness is moderate since Fetty Wap tours with some regularity, but it's still a real show at a good venue. Solid pick for the young professional segment of this audience.

event_name: Noche De Muertos at El Super Pan
blurb:
If you're the type who wants the night to keep going after dinner, El Super Pan has you covered.

Noche De Muertos is their Halloween party and it runs from 11 PM to 2 AM with DJ Dixon and DJ Hollywood on the decks. There's a costume contest with a $150 cash prize, limited-time Halloween cocktails all night, and the kind of late-night energy that El Super Pan does better than most spots in the Battery. The tagline is 'la noche es de los muertos, pero el perreo es de los vivos' which, roughly translated, means the night belongs to the dead but the dancing belongs to the living. Can't argue with that.

This one is for the folks who want to make a full night of it on Halloween. Dinner somewhere, then this. Halloween on a Saturday only happens so often. Take advantage.
scoring_notes: Good late-night option for the younger end of the Perimeter audience, young professionals without kids who want to stay out on a Saturday Halloween. The $150 costume contest prize is a nice hook. Slightly lower demographic fit than the Live! party because the 11 PM start skews younger, but still solid for this audience.

event_name: Cork & Crust: Wine and Pie Tasting
blurb:
Four wines. Four pies. One Sunday evening that gives you something to actually look forward to at the end of a weekend.

Deep Roots Wine Market on Marietta Square is hosting Cork & Crust on November 9th, pairing wines with pies from Pie Bar in a guided tasting format. If you've been to Pie Bar you already know the pies can hold their own. The wine side is in Deep Roots' hands, and they know what they're doing. At $50 a ticket for a guided experience like this, it's not a hard sell.

This is a good one for couples, good for a girls' night out, good for anyone who wants a Sunday evening that feels intentional rather than just whatever happens to be on TV. Marietta Square is a pleasant drive from the Perimeter area and worth the trip for the right event. This qualifies.

Tickets are $50. Grab them before it fills up, tasting events like this tend to sell out when the format is this dialed in.
scoring_notes: Strong fit for the educated, higher-income Perimeter audience who appreciates curated food and wine experiences. $50 is genuinely accessible at this income level. Sunday evening timing works well for this demographic. The wine-plus-artisan-food format skews adult, which matches this audience. Marietta is a short drive and familiar to many Perimeter residents.

event_name: Carl Cox at Coca-Cola Roxy
blurb:
Carl Cox is one of the most legendary DJs on the planet. If you've been to Ibiza, you already know. If you haven't, here's what you need to know: the man has been headlining festivals and clubs since the late 80s and he still sells out rooms because he's just that good.

He's coming to Coca-Cola Roxy on Friday, November 13th. The Roxy is one of the better venues in Atlanta for a night like this, good sound, good size, close to everything. A 9 PM start on a Friday means you have time for dinner before, and November 13th is far enough away from the holiday season that there's no excuse not to go.

This is a bucket-list show for anyone who takes electronic music even a little seriously. And even if you're more casual about it, there's something to be said for seeing a true original do what he does best in a room that size. It won't feel like a festival. It'll feel like a show.

Get your tickets now. Carl Cox at a venue this size in Atlanta is not a regular occurrence.
scoring_notes: Carl Cox is an iconic artist with genuine can't-miss status. Strong uniqueness score because he rarely plays rooms this small. Demographic fit is good but not perfect since electronic music skews slightly younger than the Perimeter median age. Friday night timing is ideal. The $105K income level makes ticket price a non-issue.

event_name: Live From the Dead Halloween Party at Live!
venue: Live! at The Battery Atlanta, Atlanta
blurb:
Halloween falls on a Saturday this year, and The Battery is not letting that go to waste.

Live! at The Battery is throwing a full-on haunted takeover called Live From the Dead, and it's exactly what a Halloween night out should look like. We're talking eerie decor, live DJs, roaming performers, stilt walkers, fortune tellers, costume contests with real prizes, and themed cocktails that lean hard into the season. This is not a bar that threw up some fake cobwebs and called it a party. They've built an experience around it.

If you're the kind of person who wants to actually DO something on Halloween instead of just handing out candy and calling it a night, this is your move. Dress up. Go out. The Battery is one of the better setups in Atlanta for a night like this, plenty of food and drink options, easy to navigate, and already buzzing on a normal Friday. On Halloween? It'll be something else entirely.

Grab your tickets before they're gone. Saturday Halloween nights don't come around that often.
scoring_notes: Halloween on a Saturday is genuinely rare and this event capitalizes on it. Strong fit for the 38-median-age crowd of young professionals and couples who want a night out rather than a neighborhood block party. The Battery is close enough to the Perimeter area to feel local. Adult-skewing, which matches this audience well.

event_name: Silent Night | The Atlanta Opera
venue: Cobb Energy Performing Arts Centre, Atlanta
blurb:
This one is special in a way that doesn't come around often.

Silent Night is the true story of the spontaneous Christmas truce of World War I, when French, British, and German soldiers on opposing sides laid down their weapons on Christmas Eve, came together around a makeshift tree, sang carols, and played soccer. The Atlanta Opera is staging it at the Cobb Energy Performing Arts Centre, directed by Artistic Director Tomer Zvulun, who previously directed this same production at the Wexford Festival Opera where it won the Audience Choice Award and Best Opera Award at the Irish Times Theatre Awards. The original production won the Pulitzer Prize for Music in 2012.

That's not a resume you see every week. This is a Pulitzer-winning opera, with a story that actually grabs you, in one of the best performing arts venues in metro Atlanta. It opens November 10th, which means you've got time to plan.

If you've been meaning to go to the opera but haven't found the right one to start with, Silent Night is EXACTLY the one. Buy the tickets.
scoring_notes: Exceptional fit for the educated, higher-income Perimeter audience. 70% bachelor's degree or higher is exactly the demographic that responds to Pulitzer Prize pedigree and prestigious artistic credentials. The Cobb Energy PAC is practically in the Perimeter backyard. High uniqueness because this is a critically acclaimed Pulitzer-winning production, not a standard opera season offering. Strong adult skew matches the audience.

event_name: Yebba at Coca-Cola Roxy
blurb:
If you know Yebba, you already know you need to be there. If you don't, here's the short version: she's one of the most gifted vocalists working right now, full stop.

Yebba Smith got her big moment when Ed Sheeran put her on a track and Sam Smith made her a collaborator, but anyone who's heard her perform on her own knows she doesn't need the cosign. The woman can sing in a way that doesn't feel like a performance so much as something you weren't supposed to witness. The Coca-Cola Roxy is an intimate enough room that you'll actually feel it.

This is a Thursday night, which means you either plan ahead or you miss it. Tickets at a mid-size venue for an artist at this level are absolutely worth it for the $105K household income crowd this newsletter reaches. Take a date, take a friend, take whoever in your life also thinks live music is one of the better ways to spend a weeknight.

This kind of show doesn't come to Atlanta every season. Get your tickets.
scoring_notes: Yebba is a genuinely special artist with strong crossover appeal to educated, music-literate adults in the 30-45 range. The Roxy is a great intimate venue. High uniqueness because she doesn't tour constantly. Strong fit for the adult-skewing Perimeter audience. Thursday night is a minor friction point but shouldn't be disqualifying for this income bracket.

event_name: Bladesmithing 102: Damascus Intensive
blurb: This is not a beginner class. Bladesmithing 102 is a full-day Damascus intensive where you'll layer, weld, and pattern steel using actual fire, then forge a custom knife and fork carver set with sandalwood handles. If you've done a beginner blacksmithing or knife-making session and wondered what comes next, this is the answer. Halloween day in a forge, making something sharp and handmade from raw steel. Honestly, that's a better way to spend a Saturday than most of what else is on the calendar. Seats are limited, so if this sounds like your kind of thing, don't wait.
scoring_notes: Niche but genuinely unique. Damascus bladesmithing is a real craft with a passionate following, and the East Cobb audience includes plenty of hobbyist-minded homeowners with disposable income who would find this compelling. Loses significant points on broad demographic fit and audience match because it's a narrow interest that won't resonate with most readers. Worth including because for the right subscriber, it's a PERFECT pick, and the uniqueness score is the highest in the list.

event_name: Travel Abroad with the Tritone Orchestras: A Musical World Tour
blurb: The Tritone Orchestras are taking you around the world without making you pack a bag. The program hits ABBA, Gloria Estefan, Fela Kuti, the Beatles, Grieg, Piazzolla tangos, and K-pop, which is one of the more eclectic setlists you'll see on a stage in metro Atlanta this fall. The real centerpiece of the evening is a live collaboration with Dr. Kakali Bandyopadhyay and Sri Anjaneya Sastry, who bring sitar and tabla to the stage in what the organizers describe as a rare pairing alongside a full orchestra. Roswell Cultural Arts Center is a short drive from East Cobb, the program is genuinely different from anything else on the calendar this weekend, and this Sunday it closes before the holiday season fully consumes everyone's schedule.
scoring_notes: Strong uniqueness score because the sitar and tabla pairing with full orchestra is a legitimate musical novelty, not just a themed concert. The genre-spanning program from Beatles to Fela Kuti to K-pop gives it broad appeal. Roswell is adjacent to East Cobb, so proximity is solid. Loses points because a 42-median-age audience may be less connected to some of the artists in the lineup, and the ensemble (Tritone Orchestras) is not a marquee name that drives urgency on its own.

event_name: Silent Night | The Atlanta Opera
venue: Cobb Energy Performing Arts Centre, Atlanta
blurb: If you've never gone to the opera because it felt like someone else's thing, this one might change your mind. Silent Night tells the true story of the Christmas truce of 1914, when French, British, and German soldiers laid down their weapons on Christmas Eve, gathered around a makeshift tree, sang carols, and played soccer in no man's land. Based on the film Joyeux Noel, it's a war story that becomes something else entirely. The score won the Pulitzer Prize for Music in 2012. Atlanta Opera's Artistic Director Tomer Zvulun is directing, and he previously staged this exact co-production at the Wexford Festival Opera in Ireland, where it won Best Opera and the Audience Choice Award. It's at Cobb Energy, which means you're not driving into the city. For the right person, this is a SPECIAL night out.
scoring_notes: A Pulitzer-winning opera at a nearby venue with a subject matter (WWI, Christmas truce) that has broad emotional reach is a strong fit for educated, higher-income East Cobb households. The 65% college-educated audience and $118K median income means the price point and cultural format are not a barrier. Loses a point on audience match because opera skews older even within this demographic, but the accessibility of the subject matter and the proximity of the venue offset that.

event_name: Gnarls Barkley at Coca-Cola Roxy
blurb: Gnarls Barkley. Live. That's the whole pitch. Cee Lo Green and Danger Mouse haven't toured together much, and for anyone who was in their mid-to-late 20s or 30s when "Crazy" was everywhere, seeing them live is the kind of thing you'll kick yourself for skipping. The Coca-Cola Roxy at the Battery is easy from East Cobb, parking is manageable if you go early, and a Tuesday night show means the crowd actually wants to be there. This is one of those nights where you buy the tickets first and figure out the babysitter situation second.
scoring_notes: Gnarls Barkley's peak was 2006-2008, which lands squarely in the nostalgia zone for a 42-median-age audience. This demographic was 22-24 when Crazy dropped, which means real emotional connection. The Battery is a known, easy destination for East Cobb residents. Loses a point on demographic fit because Tuesday night shows are harder for families with school-age kids, but the empty nester and couples segment of this audience doesn't have that friction.

event_name: It's a Wonderful Life: A Live Radio Play
blurb: You know the story. George Bailey, Bedford Falls, the bridge, Clarence the angel. But you haven't seen it like this. The Strand Theatre is presenting It's a Wonderful Life as a live 1940s-style radio broadcast, with a small ensemble of actors voicing dozens of characters, live foley sound effects, and vintage microphones center stage. No sets. No costumes. Just performance, craft, and imagination doing all the heavy lifting. It sounds simple. It's actually a harder thing to pull off than a full production, and when it works, it hits differently. This is Marietta's own Strand Theatre, a few minutes from home, doing something genuinely creative with material everyone already loves. Early November feels early for holiday programming, but honestly? Getting ahead of the December crush is never a bad idea.
scoring_notes: Strong match for the 42-median-age East Cobb crowd, especially the empty nester segment that grew up with this film. The radio play format gives a familiar story a fresh theatrical hook. Marietta is their backyard. Family-friendly but skews adult in its appeal, which fits the audience. Loses a point on uniqueness because It's a Wonderful Life productions run every holiday season, but the radio play format keeps it from being generic.

event_name: Duckhorn Portfolio Wine Dinner with Silla del Toro
blurb: Forty dollars for a paired wine dinner featuring Duckhorn is a genuinely good deal, and if you know the Duckhorn Portfolio at all, you already know that. Deep Roots Wine Market is hosting the evening at Silla del Toro, pairing wines from one of Napa's better-known portfolio houses with dinner. The format is relaxed, the setting is local, and the wines are the kind you'd normally uncork for a special occasion, not a Tuesday. It's a Monday night, which actually makes it easier to get a table with a good group. $40 a person, dinner included. For this audience, that's a night out worth circling.
scoring_notes: Near-perfect demographic fit. $118K median household income, educated, homeowning adults who are into food and wine. $40 is a non-issue. The Duckhorn name carries real recognition with this crowd. Loses a point on uniqueness because wine dinners happen regularly, but the Duckhorn brand and the $40 price point make it stand out within the format. Strong audience match for the empty nester and established couples segment.

event_name: Hayde Bluegrass Orchestra on Marietta Square
blurb: A seven-piece bluegrass band from Oslo, Norway playing on Marietta Square is not a sentence you read every day. Hayde Bluegrass Orchestra blends traditional American roots music with Nordic folk in a style they call "Nordicana," and it works in a way that sounds like it shouldn't. Fiddle, dobro, banjo, mandolin, accordion, four-part harmonies. The band is fronted by Rebekka Nilsson, who won the IBMA Momentum Vocalist of the Year award in 2022, so the vocals alone are worth showing up for. Opening the night are The Lonely Few, a North Georgia folk and bluegrass trio drawing from Appalachian tradition. Two bands, one square, one Thursday night that has a real chance of being the best live music you catch all fall. Doors open at 6 PM.
scoring_notes: East Cobb's median age of 42 and mix of established families and empty nesters skews toward live music with roots and character over club-style concerts. A Norwegian bluegrass band is genuinely unusual and not a recurring weekly event. Marietta Square is close, walkable, and familiar to this audience. The combination of an internationally recognized headliner and a local opener gives it range. Ticket price not specified but likely modest, which is a non-issue for a $118K household.

event_name: Fall Colors Canoe Trips
blurb:
The Chattahoochee doesn't look like this for long. Right now, the tree canopy along the river corridor is doing its full fall thing, and the Nature Center is running guided canoe trips so you can actually be in it instead of just driving past it on 400.

You'll paddle out in the late afternoon, which means golden light on the water and the kind of quiet that's genuinely hard to find around here. Wildlife tends to come out around this time of day too. It's ages 8 and up, so if you've got a teenager who needs to put the phone down for three hours, this is a solid excuse. And if it's just you and your person looking for something that isn't another restaurant, this works even better.

At $45 a head, it's nothing. Spots will fill. Go get on the water before the leaves are gone.
scoring_notes: Peak fall foliage canoe trips have a narrow seasonal window, making this genuinely time-sensitive. At $45, it's a non-issue for a $118K household. Works perfectly for the mix of established families with older kids and empty nesters who want an active, outdoor experience. The Chattahoochee Nature Center is practically in East Cobb's backyard.

event_name: Weaving Demo: The Wild Wild Weft
blurb:
The name alone deserves some credit. The Wild Wild Weft is a two-hour weaving demonstration that runs Saturday afternoon, and it's the kind of hands-on, craft-focused event that tends to be way more interesting in person than it sounds on paper.

If you've got kids who are curious about making things, or you're into fiber arts, or you just want something genuinely different from your usual Saturday afternoon, this fills a gap. It's free, it's indoors, and it's a good option to slot between the morning car show and the evening Halloween events without burning out before the main event.
scoring_notes: Lower mass appeal but high uniqueness score. Arts and crafts demos skew toward families with curious kids and creative adults. Fits the educated demographic profile (50% bachelor's degree or higher). Low stakes, low cost, and fills the afternoon gap on Saturday. Included to give variety in the lineup rather than stacking four near-identical event types.

event_name: Acoustic Jam Session
blurb:
Friday night, live acoustic music, three hours. If you need more than that to decide, you might be overthinking it.

Acoustic sets are low-key in the best way. No overwhelming volume, no cover charge, no pressure to stay for a full concert arc. You can grab dinner nearby, drift in when it's already going, and just let the weekend start the right way. This is a solid option for couples looking for something easy or a small group that wants to actually be able to have a conversation while there's music playing.

Kick the weekend off right. It's free and it starts at 6.
scoring_notes: Recurring events are generally lower priority, but this fills a Friday night adult slot that no other candidate covers. The audience skews 36 median age with dual-income households who want low-effort, low-cost weeknight options. Works for the Flower Mound and Highland Village crowd looking for something easy after the work week. Included because Friday coverage matters and this is the only Friday candidate.

event_name: The Rocky Horror Picture Show Film Screening
blurb:
Look, if you've never seen Rocky Horror in a room full of people who actually know what to do during a screening, you're missing something. This is not a movie you watch quietly. People dress up, shout callbacks at the screen, and generally commit in a way that makes a regular Saturday night at home feel embarrassing by comparison.

Halloween week is the only time of year this one really makes sense, and it's happening Saturday night. The college-adjacent crowd near UNT and TWU will feel right at home here. But honestly anyone who enjoys a little chaos with their cult classics should show up in costume and see what happens.

It starts at 8:00 PM. Come ready to participate.
scoring_notes: Seasonal uniqueness is high since Rocky Horror screenings are essentially a Halloween-only tradition. Strong fit for the younger, college-adjacent segment of the audience and adults who want something that isn't a kids event. Lower family match but that's fine since Little Monsters on Main covers that lane. Good balance in the lineup.

event_name: EsDeeKid at Coca-Cola Roxy
blurb: EsDeeKid hits the Coca-Cola Roxy this Saturday night for a show that runs through 11:30pm. The Roxy is one of the better mid-size venues in Atlanta and it's right at The Battery, so you've got a full night if you want it: dinner before, show, and a place to land after without ever moving your car twice. This is a solid Saturday-night-out option for the crowd that wants live music without a stadium production. Doors open at 7, so get there early if you want to actually be in the room for the start.
scoring_notes: The Roxy is close to the Perimeter coverage area and The Battery is a familiar destination for this demographic. EsDeeKid is a niche pick that may not land with the full audience, but the venue and Saturday timing are strong. Included because it's the only music concert this weekend within reasonable distance.

event_name: Amp It Up Live Music Festival featuring Heart of Atlanta
blurb: Heart of Atlanta, Atlanta's top Heart tribute band, headlines a full outdoor music festival in Roswell this Saturday. The event pulls in local musicians and bands throughout the afternoon and doubles as a fundraiser for Perfect Harmony Health's music therapy scholarship program, which helps individuals with disabilities access music therapy regardless of what they can afford. So you get a great afternoon of live music and the money goes somewhere real. If you've never heard Heart played live by people who actually take it seriously, this is your chance. Roswell Junction is a good outdoor space and October weather is about as good as it gets for this kind of thing.
scoring_notes: Broad appeal, charitable angle adds depth, outdoor festival format works for families and adults alike. Heart tribute band skews slightly older which fits the 38-median-age crowd. Not the highest uniqueness but the cause component gives it more weight than a generic music festival.

event_name: Travel Abroad with the Tritone Orchestras: A Musical World Tour
blurb: The Sunday after Halloween can go one of two ways. This is the good version. Tritone Orchestras is putting on a two-hour world music tour at the Roswell Cultural Arts Center on November 1st, working through genres and musical traditions from across multiple continents in one afternoon. It's a family-friendly option that doesn't feel like you're dragging anyone anywhere, because the concept is genuinely interesting. Music from 20-something countries in a single sit-down performance is not a normal Sunday afternoon, and the Roswell Cultural Arts Center is one of the better venues in the area for this kind of thing. Grab tickets and make the day worthwhile.
scoring_notes: Family-friendly but adult-appealing, fits the mix of young families and empty nesters in the Perimeter audience. November 1st (post-Halloween Sunday) is a good slot with low competition. The world tour concept is more interesting than a standard orchestra performance, which lifts the uniqueness score.

event_name: Lumiere Lounge Jazz Talks with Trey Wright
venue: Earl and Rachel Smith Strand Theatre, Marietta
blurb: KSU Professor Trey Wright is doing something genuinely interesting at the Strand Theatre in Marietta on November 5th. It's not a concert. It's a jazz talk, 30 people max, one drink ticket included, doors at 7pm with the presentation at 7:30. This edition is on Charlie Christian and the evolution of jazz guitar, which is one of those corners of music history that feels obscure until someone walks you through it and suddenly you can't believe you didn't know it sooner. Thirty seats. Adults only (21+). The kind of Thursday night that's worth rescheduling dinner for.
scoring_notes: High education level in this audience makes a professor-led jazz history talk a genuinely good fit. 30-seat cap creates real scarcity. Adult-only format matches the more adult-skewing Perimeter audience. Thursday publish window means this lands with enough lead time to act on it.

event_name: Blacksmithing Skulls with Michael Dillon
blurb: You're going to forge an iron skull. That's the thing. Local artist Michael Dillon, known for large-scale architectural metalwork, is teaching a hands-on blacksmithing session at Art Center West in Roswell this Saturday. You'll work with raw iron, use real tools, and walk out with something you actually made with your hands. It's Halloween-adjacent in the best possible way, and it's the kind of Saturday afternoon that zero percent of your coworkers will have had. Seats are limited by the nature of the space, so if this sounds like your kind of afternoon, don't sit on it.
scoring_notes: High uniqueness score, skilled-instructor-led experience, Halloween timing with the skull theme. Fits the educated, experience-seeking demographic well. Lower demographic fit than bar crawl or dinner party because it's niche, but that niche is strong and the audience can afford it.

event_name: Emo Night and Halloween Party
blurb: If you spent any part of your teens or early twenties listening to My Chemical Romance or Fall Out Boy with the lights off, this one's going to hit. Rock 'N' Taco in Roswell is throwing a Halloween-themed emo night on October 29th with live throwback performances from Pop Rocks ATL. It's early enough in the week that it's not competing with Halloween Saturday, which means the crowd will be smaller and the vibe will be better. Show up in costume or don't, but either way come ready to sing every word to songs you thought you'd forgotten. Starts at 8pm.
scoring_notes: Median age of 38 puts a big chunk of this audience squarely in the emo-era nostalgia zone (early 2000s). Adult-skewing, low barrier to entry, social and fun without being a massive production. The Halloween angle adds seasonal relevance.

event_name: Roswell Boos & Booze Halloween Bar Crawl
blurb: Halloween falls on a Saturday this year, which means the bar crawl situation in Roswell is going to be loud, costumed, and worth showing up for. The 3rd Annual Boos & Booze crawl runs from 3pm to 10pm through Canton Street and the surrounding spots, so you get a full evening without being locked into one venue all night. This is the kind of event that's better with a group. Round up whoever you've been meaning to make plans with, commit to a group costume, and make a night of it. Seven hours of downtown Roswell on Halloween is hard to beat.
scoring_notes: Halloween on a Saturday is a once-every-few-years occurrence that elevates what would otherwise be a recurring event. Adult-skewing, social, fits the young professional and young-family-without-kids-tonight crowd well. Roswell is close enough to Perimeter to be worth the drive for this one.

event_name: "It's Showtime!" A Beetlejuice Dinner Party
venue: Mise en Place Cooking Studio, Roswell
blurb: Halloween is five days away and this one is genuinely different. Mise en Place Cooking Studio in Roswell is throwing a hands-on dinner party inspired by Beetlejuice, and you're not just eating the food, you're making it. The whole thing is interactive, themed from start to finish, and runs just 2.5 hours so it's a real weeknight option without blowing up your Thursday morning. For a $105K household audience that's done the standard haunted house circuit about a dozen times, a cooking class where the menu is the costume is a breath of weird, fresh air. It sells out fast. Don't wait on it.
scoring_notes: High uniqueness, adult-skewing, fits the educated professional crowd that wants experiences over passive entertainment. Halloween timing is perfect for the newsletter window. Cooking studio events tend to sell limited seats, which adds genuine urgency.

event_name: Dueling Pianos at Park Bench
blurb:
No cover. No setlist. Just two pianists going at it for three hours while the crowd decides what gets played. Dueling Pianos at Park Bench in The Battery is the kind of Saturday night that starts as 'we'll just stay for one drink' and ends at midnight.

The show runs 8:30 to 11:30pm. General seating is first-come, first-served and it fills up, so if you're going with a group, reserving a table ahead of time is the smarter move. The Battery makes it easy to grab dinner somewhere first and walk over.

Free admission, good energy, and a crowd that's actually there to have fun. Hard to argue with that on a Saturday night in October.
scoring_notes: No-cover Saturday night entertainment at The Battery is very accessible for this demographic. Interactive format skews adult and social, fits young professionals well. Lower uniqueness score because Dueling Pianos is a recurring Saturday event, not a one-off. Still included because the entertainment value and zero cost are strong selling points for this audience.
